title: Candidate theory assemblies, maturity rails, and calibration control
unit: A prototype assembly is a deterministic coverage envelope over selected cells, not a composed theory.

interface_vocabulary.meaning: Both cells have been shown to use the same mathematical object with the same scope.
A proved, reversible translation connects the objects used by the two cells.
A proved bridge exists once explicitly named extra assumptions are supplied.
A quantitative approximation theorem connects the cells with an explicit error bound.
A concrete bridge has been proposed but is not certified.
A scoped obstruction proves that these particular objects cannot be joined as proposed.
No registered record currently decides how the two selected cells compose.

calibration_controls.label: Standard general relativity: observational-domain control
calibration_controls.scope: A calibration control showing that the atlas can distinguish registered predictions and successful empirical comparisons from missing records. It is not selected from the foundations cube and is not a candidate Weyl-gravity assembly.

rail_summary.basis: Four primary-source records identify a GR prediction in three benchmark families.
Each record names the measured observable and comparison domain.
The cited analyses report consistency with the tested GR prediction within their stated scope.
Independent solar-system, binary-pulsar, gravitational-wave, and multimessenger analyses test distinct regimes; this is not a universal out-of-sample theorem.

records.citation: B. Bertotti, L. Iess, and P. Tortora, A test of general relativity using radio links with the Cassini spacecraft, Nature 425, 374-376 (2003).
records.observable_map: Radio-frequency shifts during solar conjunction constrain the post-Newtonian light-time-delay parameter gamma.
records.dataset: Cassini spacecraft radio links around the 2002 solar conjunction.
records.prediction: The standard-GR value of the post-Newtonian parameter gamma.
records.comparison_method: Relativistic Doppler/time-delay fit with plasma-noise suppression.
records.uncertainty: Use the uncertainty and systematic model reported by the source; this ledger does not recompute the fit.
records.parameter_fit_scope: Solar-system weak-field propagation with nuisance/systematic modelling as specified in the source.
records.finding: The reported estimate is consistent with the standard-GR prediction within the experiment's stated uncertainty.
records.boundary: Does not test strong-field dynamics, gravitational radiation, galactic phenomenology, cosmology, quantum gravity, or a foundations-cube composition map.

records.citation: M. Kramer et al., Strong-Field Gravity Tests with the Double Pulsar, Physical Review X 11, 041050 (2021).
records.observable_map: Relativistic timing parameters and orbital decay map to conservative and radiative strong-field predictions.
records.dataset: Sixteen years of timing observations of PSR J0737-3039A/B.
records.prediction: Multiple post-Keplerian relations and the GR quadrupolar gravitational-radiation prediction for the double-pulsar system.
records.comparison_method: Joint pulsar-timing model with propagation, kinematic, and mass-loss corrections described in the source.
records.uncertainty: The source reports validation of the GR quadrupolar radiation prediction at 1.3e-4 (95% confidence).
records.parameter_fit_scope: A specific relativistic binary system under the timing and correction model in the paper.
records.finding: The tested post-Keplerian and radiative predictions are mutually consistent with GR at the reported precision.
records.boundary: A high-precision strong-field binary test, not a proof of GR in arbitrary compact objects, cosmology, or the quantum domain.

records.citation: LIGO Scientific Collaboration, Virgo Collaboration, and KAGRA Collaboration, Tests of General Relativity with GWTC-3, arXiv:2112.06861 (2021).
records.observable_map: Compact-binary gravitational-wave phase, amplitude, residual, polarization, dispersion, and remnant-consistency observables map to parameterized deviations from GR.
records.dataset: The confident compact-binary coalescences used by the GWTC-3 general-relativity tests.
records.prediction: GR waveform generation and propagation, tested through multiple parameterized and residual analyses.
records.comparison_method: A suite of waveform-consistency, residual, polarization, dispersion, and parameterized-deviation analyses.
records.uncertainty: Analysis-specific credible intervals and systematic qualifications are those reported in the source.
records.parameter_fit_scope: The event populations, waveform models, priors, and analysis selections specified in the source.
records.finding: The reported tests find no evidence for deviations from GR in the analysed GWTC-3 signals.
records.boundary: Consistency within the analysed catalogue and waveform systematics is not proof of GR for every source, propagation environment, polarization model, or cosmological history.

records.citation: B. P. Abbott et al., Gravitational Waves and Gamma-rays from a Binary Neutron Star Merger: GW170817 and GRB 170817A, Astrophysical Journal Letters 848, L13 (2017).
records.observable_map: The gravitational-wave/gamma-ray arrival-time difference constrains relative propagation speed and violations of gravitational versus electromagnetic propagation.
records.prediction: Near-luminal gravitational-wave propagation and the associated arrival-time relation, modulo source-emission delay.
records.comparison_method: Bound propagation differences using the observed arrival delay and stated assumptions about emission timing and distance.
records.uncertainty: The source's bounds are conditional on the stated source-delay and propagation assumptions.
records.parameter_fit_scope: One multimessenger binary-neutron-star event and its source-model assumptions.
records.finding: The observed delay yields stringent bounds compatible with standard luminal GR propagation in the tested setting.
records.boundary: Does not isolate all modified-gravity effects, determine waveform generation by itself, or provide a universal propagation theorem.
